Container.Name: claude-code-linux
Container.Changes: Rebased on LinuxServer.io's baseimage-selkies: PUID/PGID 99/100 and UMASK work natively, state moves to /config, ports are 3000 (HTTP) and 3001 (HTTPS). This is a fresh start: point AppData at a new, empty folder and sign in to Claude once more.
Container.Overview:
Claude Desktop and Claude Code in your web browser.
First, once in the Unraid terminal: docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR-GITHUB-USERNAME (password: a GitHub token with read:packages).
• Set Workspace to the folder with your projects. Leave the rest as it is. • From outside your home: point your reverse proxy (for example Pangolin) at port 3000. At home: open https://YOUR-SERVER-IP:3001 and accept the certificate warning once. • There is no desktop password; your reverse proxy is the lock. Never open 3000 or 3001 to the Internet directly. • Your sign-ins and settings live in AppData and survive updates. • Upgrading from the old version? Use a new, empty AppData folder and sign in again once.

Config.Name: WebUI Port (HTTPS / Selkies)
Config.Description: HTTPS port of the Selkies WebUI with a self-signed certificate, for use on the LAN; accept the certificate once.

Config.Name: WebUI Port (HTTP / Selkies)
Config.Description: HTTP port of the Selkies WebUI, for the reverse proxy (Pangolin) that terminates TLS and authenticates in front of the container.

Config.Name: AppData (/config)
Config.Description: Persistent desktop state: Claude Desktop's sign-in and settings, the keyring, the Chrome profile and the Claude Code CLI credentials.

Config.Name: Workspace (/workspaces)
Config.Description: Optional. A host folder with your projects, shown inside the container at /workspaces.

Config.Name: Timezone (TZ)
Config.Description: Container timezone as an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin.

Config.Name: User ID (PUID)
Config.Description: User ID the desktop runs as. Default 99 (nobody on Unraid).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Permission mask for new files. The default 002 keeps them writable for the users group, which suits shares that other containers touch too.
